​​​This time, we're back at **Delve's** office on Arch Street.

​*Hardware Meetups happen across 30+ cities monthly and help bring together different professionals to connect and meet each other.*

​**We will have a great set of featured speakers for the evening!:**

* ​[Dan Lykens](https://www.linkedin.com/in/danlykens/?utm_source=luma), Electromechanical Engineer at [Production Systems Automation](https://www.psasystems.com/?utm_source=luma). Dan is a multidisciplinary engineer and entrepreneur with over a decade of experience in electromechanical systems, PCB design, and product development. At PSA, he leads defense-focused R&D projects, specializing in rugged electronics. Dan combines deep technical proficiency in PCB design, CAD modeling, and advanced prototyping techniques.
* ​[David Levine](https://www.linkedin.com/in/david-j-levine/), Senior Solutions Engineer, [Viam](https://viam.com). Viam is a software platform for building, deploying, and managing robotics applications. Viam brings software engineering practices to robotics: version control, remote monitoring and diagnostics, staged rollouts, and a registry of modules and models you can build on. At Viam, David is one of the leaders of robotic solution design -- including hardware, electronics, safety systems, and supporting software -- for automation customers across various industries. Prior to joining Viam, David received his Ph.D. in Mechanical Engineering from UPenn in 2023 and B.S. in Mechanical Engineering from Cornell in 2017, and previously founded a robotics startup in the Philadelphia ecosystem, which was later supported by the Cornell Tech Runway Postdoctoral Fellowship.
* [Daniel Marcq](https://www.linkedin.com/in/daniel-marcq-jr/), Client Partner and Senior Director of Electrical & Software Engineering at [Delve](http://www.delve.com/). Dan leads the development of complex hardware and connected systems from early strategy through commercialization. Since joining Delve in 2019, he has led multidisciplinary programs spanning electrical engineering, embedded systems, robotics, sensing, controls, and software for medical devices and other advanced products.

​**Thank you to our partners!:**

​We’re excited to welcome **[Efinix](https://www.efinixinc.com/index.html?utm_source=luma)** as a sponsor of our next Philadelphia Hardware Meetup!
Efinix manufactures the world’s most efficient FPGAs. Delivering low power, high performance and small physical size, Efinix FPGAs offer fast time to market in a cost-effective footprint. Efinix offers three families of FPGAs from the entry level Trion family that prioritizes I/O and connectivity to the Titanium family that offer high speed transceivers and high compute capability for industrial, edge and highly accelerated AI applications. The portfolio spans 4,000 logic elements up 375,000 logic elements and includes SiP offering with Flash and system memory in the same FPGA package. These highly integrated solutions reduce design complexity, increase available I/O and further speed time to market. The Efinix Efinity tool suite is freely available and delivers an intuitive RTL to bit-stream capability while supporting a rich IP library and software compilers for the suite of Sapphire RISC-V processors available as both hard IP and soft macros across the Efinix portfolio.
Efinix FPGAs have been widely adopted in a broad array of markets from industrial automation , communications, medical, automotive and test and measurement. To find out more about Efinix products and markets, visit [www.efinixinc.com](http://www.efinixinc.com/ "http://www.efinixinc.com").
Thank you to Efinix for supporting the Philadelphia hardware community and helping bring local engineers, founders, and product developers together.

BFTP creates and retains highly paid, sustainable jobs by investing in and linking early-stage technology firms and established manufacturers with experts, universities, follow-on funding, and other resources to help them prosper through innovation.

name: AI Agent Hackathon!
description:
# 🤖 AI Agent Hackathon

## Two Days Two Locations One Hackathon

Join Coffee & Code Philadelphia for a hands-on, in-person hackathon focused on building, experimenting with, and shipping working AI-agent projects.
The main Hackathon Build Day takes place on September 20 at Pennovation Center. Projects, winners, and members of Philadelphia’s AI community will come together again on September 22 for an expanded Awards & Community Night at Cesium.
Come with a team, meet collaborators at the event, or build independently. You do not need to arrive with a finished project idea.

## 👤 Who Should Attend

This event is for developers, engineers, technical builders, founders, researchers, students, and anyone interested in experimenting with AI-agent systems.
Whether you already work with agent frameworks or are just beginning to explore them, the goal is to test ideas, learn from other builders, and leave with something working.
You may participate:

* With an existing team
* By finding collaborators at the event
* As an independent builder
* Without a finished project idea

## 🧠 What You Can Build

Projects may explore:

* Coding agents
* Multi-agent systems
* Tool use and automation
* Agent memory and context
* Evaluation and reliability
* AI safety and security
* Open-source agent frameworks
* Real-world agent applications
* Sponsor challenge tracks
* The Open Track and Bring Your Own Project

## 📅 Day 1 Hackathon Build Day

**Sunday, September 20, 2026**
**Pennovation Center**
3401 Grays Ferry Avenue
Philadelphia, PA 19146

### Schedule

**9:00–9:40 AM** — Registration and check-in
**10:00–10:15 AM** — Opening ceremony
**10:15–10:30 AM** — Challenge track introductions
**10:32–10:35 AM** — Quirq
**10:37–10:40 AM** — The Code Registry
**10:42–10:45 AM** — GalaxyGate
**10:47–10:50 AM** — Human Standard
**10:52–10:55 AM** — Naftiko
**10:57–11:00 AM** — Open Track and Bring Your Own Project
**11:00 AM–6:00 PM** — Hackathon build time

## 🏆 Day 2 Awards and Community Night

**Tuesday, September 22, 2026**
**Cesium**
601 Walnut Street, Suite 250S
Philadelphia, PA 19106
We have extended the evening until 9:00 PM to provide more time for project demos, conversations with the builders, and networking after the awards.

### Schedule

**6:00 PM** — Doors, pizza, and hackathon demo booths
**6:30 PM** — Welcome introductions
**6:40 PM** — Main talk by Tom DiCarlo of Bentley Systems on AI Gateway Infrastructure
**7:05 PM** — Lightning talks featuring short AI demos from local builders
**7:35 PM** — Hackathon awards and closing ceremony
**8:00–9:00 PM** — Post-awards networking and final project demos

## 🎒 What to Bring

* A laptop and charger
* Your preferred development environment
* Any API keys, accounts, datasets, or tools you plan to use
* Your project idea, if you have one

Please configure and test your development tools before arriving so you can spend more time building.

## 📦 Submission Requirements

To be eligible for judging, each team or solo builder must submit:

* A working prototype that meaningfully uses AI agents or agentic workflows
* A description of the problem, project, and use of AI agents
* A source-code repository
* A demo video of three minutes or less
* A list of the models, frameworks, APIs, tools, and datasets used
* A complete team-member list
* Setup or reproduction instructions
* A clear explanation of what was created or significantly extended during the hackathon

Projects should be substantially built during the hackathon. Existing libraries, APIs, models, frameworks, boilerplate, and general-purpose tools may be used.
A polished production application is not required. Judges should be able to understand the idea, see a functioning prototype, and evaluate how AI agents are used.

## 🏆 Challenge Tracks

Participating tracks include:

* Quirq
* The Code Registry
* GalaxyGate
* Human Standard
* Open Track and Bring Your Own Project

Each sponsor track has its own challenge, judging criteria, submission requirements, and award.

name: Hiring Talent and Getting Hired in an AI-Driven Market
description:
Join fellow ProductTank members and a panel of career and recruiting experts from Computer Enterprises, Inc. for a conversation about how AI is reshaping the hiring process from both sides of the table.

Whether you’re a hiring manager trying to understand how the candidate experience and talent landscape are changing, a product professional navigating your own career, or simply curious about how AI is influencing recruiting and hiring, you’ll come away with new perspectives and practical takeaways.

***Some of the areas we’ll explore:***

* How AI is changing the job search and candidate hunt
* Using AI for resumes, LinkedIn profiles, and interview preparation
* What recruiters are paying attention to
* How hiring managers might evolve their hiring process
* How candidates can stand out in a crowded market
* What AI can help with and where human judgment still matters
* Common misconceptions about recruiting and AI
* How recruiters are using AI today, including some of CEI’s experiences and lessons learned

***Event Info:***

* **When:** Wednesday, October 7th, 2026
* **Time:** 6:00-8:30 PM ET
* **Location:** CEI Plymouth Meeting Office
* **Address:** **[660 W Germantown Pike](https://www.google.com/maps/search/660+W+Germantown+Pike?entry=gmail&source=g),** Suite LL100, Plymouth Meeting, PA 19462

***Event Schedule:***

* **6:00–6:30 PM:** Networking
* **6:30–7:30 PM:** Panel discussion and Q&A
* **7:30–8:30 PM:** Networking and farewell

***About Our Partner & Sponsor****:*
CEI is an AI platform engineering firm that helps organizations build and scale digital products, modernize technology platforms, and unlock value from data and AI. We partner with enterprise teams across product, engineering, data, and technology to accelerate innovation, improve delivery, and bring new capabilities to market faster. In addition to our engineering and consulting services, CEI helps organizations attract, hire, and retain top technology talent through specialized recruiting and workforce solutions. By combining technology expertise with talent solutions, CEI helps organizations move from strategy to execution and achieve measurable business outcomes.

***About Our Panelists:***
Our ProductTank Organizer Joshua Aversa will moderate the conversation between:

* **Matthew Linneman**
*VP, Key Accounts & Recruiting, CEI*
Matthew Linneman is Vice President of Key Accounts & Recruiting at CEI, where he has spent more than 16 years helping organizations build high-performing technology teams and scale strategic client partnerships. Throughout his tenure, he has held leadership roles spanning sales, staffing, recruiting, and business development, and today leads CEI’s recruiting and key account organizations with a focus on talent strategy, growth, and innovation.

* **Matthew Pribbernow**
*Senior Team Lead, CEI*
Matthew Pribbernow is a Senior Team Lead at CEI with nearly 10 years of experience helping organizations attract, hire, and retain top technology talent. He leads recruiting initiatives across a wide range of technical disciplines and partners closely with both hiring leaders and candidates to build teams that support innovation and business growth.

* **Katie Dougherty**
*Senior Professional Recruiter, CEI*
Katie Dougherty is a Senior Professional Recruiter at CEI with more than five years of experience helping technology professionals connect with opportunities that align with their skills and career goals. She works closely with both candidates and hiring managers and brings firsthand insight into today’s evolving technology job market, hiring trends, and candidate expectations.

We hope you’ll join us for a practical and candid conversation about navigating the increasingly AI-influenced product talent market!

University of the Sciences in Philadelphia (USP)

name: RSVP to the next Philly RHUG!
description:
**REGISTER HERE: [https://reg.experiences.redhat.com/flow/redhat/4900050/rhexpressregistration/page/expressregistration?sc_cid=RHCTN1260000495451](https://reg.experiences.redhat.com/flow/redhat/4900050/rhexpressregistration/page/expressregistration?sc_cid=RHCTN1260000495451)**

In recent months, AI has fundamentally reshaped cybersecurity. Automated tooling now discovers open-source vulnerabilities and generates exploits at unprecedented speeds. As the sheer volume and velocity of CVE disclosures overwhelm traditional workflows, IT and security teams face a daunting challenge: How do you patch rapidly without destabilizing mission-critical production environments?
Join us for the next [Philadelphia Red Hat User Group (RHUG)](https://reg.experiences.redhat.com/flow/redhat/4900050/rhexpressregistration/page/expressregistration?sc_cid=RHCTN1260000495451) to explore how Red Hat turns the tide on AI-driven threats by securing the software supply chain from code to deployment.
What we'll cover:

* Red Hat Trusted Libraries: How cryptographically signed, SLSA-compliant binaries neutralize upstream risks before code hits production.
* Project Lightwell: How automated, validated patching and backports maintain enterprise stability in an AI-accelerated threat landscape.
* Peer Networking: Connect with local IT leaders and Red Hat experts over food and drinks at Philly's newest high-energy venue.

[Event Details:](https://reg.experiences.redhat.com/flow/redhat/4900050/rhexpressregistration/page/expressregistration?sc_cid=RHCTN1260000495451)

* Date: Tuesday, November 3, 2026
* Time: 3:00 PM – 6:00 PM ET
* Location: F1 Arcade Philadelphia \| 1330 Chestnut St\, Philadelphia\, PA 19107

Don't miss this opportunity to transform your security posture while networking with industry peers.
Have questions? Reach out to us at rhug@redhat.com.
We look forward to seeing you there!
Best regards,
The Red Hat User Group Team
